gap.behavioural_impact: In a period format the modern card ignores ATK boosts on the Fiend and Rock materials when setting its own ATK, and lets its controller decline the position change on every attack declaration, where the Edison-era card counted the materials' field ATK and forced all opposing Defense Position monsters face-up Attack Position.

review.notes:
Era text at the Edison snapshot is v1 (DP06-EN010, 2008-01-26); v0 (GLAS-EN040, 2007-11-14) differs only by parenthesising the Flip-effect reminder, so the chain starts at v1. Trailing cosmetic step after the recorded change, not entered as a change: v3 (LDS3-EN029, 2022-07-21, what the pinned cards.cdb text matches) writes '1 Fiend monster + 1 Rock monster', 'becomes' for 'is equal to', and trims 'and cannot be Special Summoned by other ways' - the standard redundancy trim, not a loosening; official/c58332301.lua still carries EFFECT_SPSUMMON_CONDITION with aux.EvilHeroLimit alongside c:EnableReviveLimit(), so the Dark Fusion-only restriction remains strict in every version. This card has no upstream historical or unofficial variant of any kind.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Evil HERO Dark Gaia). No period ruling in the corpus settles a claimed difference, so the functional call stands unchanged (`unresolved` at both snapshots); the search is recorded in the check. Verdicts: [event] d1 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu; d2 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu.

effective.basis: TCG release of Legendary Collection 2: The Duel Academy Years Mega Pack (LCGX-EN069), the first printing carrying the errata'd text

event.historical_text: 1 Fiend-Type monster + 1 Rock-Type monsterThis monster cannot be Special Summoned except with "Dark Fusion". The original ATK of this card is equal to the combined ATK of the Fusion Material Monsters used to Fusion Summon it. When this card declares an attack, change all Defense Position monsters your opponent controls to face-up Attack Position. Flip Effects are not activated at this time.
event.modern_text: 1 Fiend-Type monster + 1 Rock-Type monsterMust be Special Summoned with "Dark Fusion" and cannot be Special Summoned by other ways. The original ATK of this card is equal to the combined original ATK of the Fusion Material Monsters used to Fusion Summon it. When this card declares an attack: You can change all Defense Position monsters your opponent controls to face-up Attack Position. (Flip Effects are not activated at this time.)
event.summary: Two behavioural changes arrived in one printing. First, the ATK-setting clause gained 'original': the era text sets Dark Gaia's original ATK to 'the combined ATK of the Fusion Material Monsters used to Fusion Summon it', i.e. their ATK as boosted on the field at the moment of the Fusion Summon, whereas v2 onward say 'combined original ATK' and official/c58332301.lua sums the materials' ATK from c:GetMaterial() after they have been sent to the Graveyard, where field ATK modifications no longer apply. Second, the attack-declaration position change became optional: 'When this card declares an attack, change all Defense Position monsters your opponent controls to face-up Attack Position' was mandatory, while v2 reads 'You can change ...' and the script registers it as EFFECT_TYPE_TRIGGER_O on EVENT_ATTACK_ANNOUNCE.

rulings_check.difference: The era card sets its original ATK to the combined ATK of the materials as they stood on the field at the Fusion Summon (boosts included); the modern card sums the materials' original ATK (script reads them from the Graveyard). The era attack-declaration position change is mandatory; the modern one is optional ('You can change ...').
